def AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess.{u_1} : {Omega :
    Type u_1} →
  {m : MeasurableSpace Omega} →
    {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal m} →
      {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure Omega} →
        {T : NNReal} →
          {B : NNReal → Omega → ℝ} →
            [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure mu] →
              AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu
                  T →
                0 < T →
                  AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B
                      filtration mu →
                    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions
                        filtration mu →
                      NNReal → Omega → ℝ :=
fun {Omega} {m} {filtration} {mu} {T} {B} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure mu] eta hT _hB _hUsual t omega =>
  if omega ∈ AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.uniformBadSet eta hT B then 0
  else AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.canonicalPathLimit eta hT B t omega
The underlying canonicalItoProcess is the sequence of elementary stochastic integrals of the chosen progressively measurable L² approximations on [0,T]. uniformBadSet is the complement of their uniform Cauchy event, proved μ-null under the Brownian assumptions. canonicalPathLimit is their pointwise limit; this defines the continuous completed Itô integral, patched to zero on that exceptional set and held constant after T. At each fixed t≤T it agrees almost everywhere with the L²-completion integral of the integrand restricted to [0,t]. These are characterization facts for interpreting this defined object, not hypotheses of the target.

structure ProbabilityTheory.IsBrownianReal.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (X : NNReal → Ω → ℝ)
  (P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop
number of parameters: 4
parents:
  ProbabilityTheory.IsBrownianReal.toIsPreBrownianReal : ProbabilityTheory.IsPreBrownianReal X P
fields:
  ProbabilityTheory.IsPreBrownianReal.hasLaw : ∀ (I : Finset NNReal),
      ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (fun ω => I.restrict fun x => X x ω) (ProbabilityTheory.BrownianReal.projectiveFamily I)
        P
  ProbabilityTheory.IsBrownianReal.cont : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂P, Continuous fun x => X x ω

The finite-dimensional family ProbabilityTheory.BrownianReal.projectiveFamily I is the centered Gaussian on real coordinates indexed by the finite time set I, with covariance (i,j) ↦ min(i,j). Consequently the scalar IsBrownianReal predicate fixes the standard Brownian finite-dimensional distributions (including X₀=0 almost surely) and requires almost-sure continuous paths. It does not require X₀=0 for every sample.

In SatisfiesUsualConditions the completeAt field is ∀ t s, μ s = 0 → MeasurableSet[filtration t] s. Thus every null set belongs to every time sigma-algebra, not just the ambient one; the other field is right continuity of the filtration.
